candidate.title: TCR-LA-MC / PCR
candidate.scope: The middle TCR-LA-MC PCR row of the assigned Illumina poster crop, interpreted as the Illumina/MiSeq library interface of TCR ligation-anchored-magnetically captured PCR described in PMID 26324409. The card slash and line break do not denote separate methods: the diagram expands one method name. Visible inventory: RNA with a C segment; constant-gene-primed cDNA; RNA digestion; ssDNA linker ligation and magnetic-bead attachment; PCR 1 with a bead; PCR 2 with nested primers; adapter addition; indexed P5/P7 DNA ready for sequencing. The top TCR Chain Pairing row and bottom CirSeq row are separate neighboring entries, with no material-transfer arrows into this route, and are outside this card. There is one representative TCR-chain route, not an explicit split or pooling branch. Capture and the between-round strand transfer are made explicit only to explain consequential attachment changes, using the matching primary method. This record does not extract the paper’s RACE comparisons, 454 interface or other unshown adaptations; it stops at library DNA and does not add a sequencing/analysis operation.

operations.description: Use the RNA constant-gene region as the priming anchor and synthesize a TCR DNA copy; the product contains the RNA template paired with biotinylated cDNA.

operations.information_effect: Transfers expressed TCR sequence information to a DNA carrier while adding a capture handle at a known constant-region site.

operations.label: Magnetic capture (within the ssDNA linker ligation block)
operations.description: Immobilize the biotinylated cDNA on streptavidin magnetic beads before linker ligation. The bead-bearing ligation product in the poster compresses this capture into the ligation block.
operations.mechanism: Capture through biotin–streptavidin association, as identified by the primary paper; the bead is an attachment/capture reagent, not a biological compartment.
operations.information_effect: Enriches the biotin-labelled cDNA population and changes its attachment state. Capture of a labelled molecule does not by itself prove that every retained molecule is a specific TCR target.

operations.label: ssDNA linker ligation
operations.description: Covalently append the known ssDNA linker cassette to the free 3′ end of the captured cDNA, opposite its constant-region capture handle.
operations.mechanism: The primary implementation specifies CircLigase and a 5′-phosphorylated, 3′-dideoxycytidine-terminated ssLC. This is addition of a DNA linker to cDNA, not RNA circularization.
operations.information_effect: Adds a known priming site adjacent to the copied unknown TCR variable sequence. Amplification is anchored by the constant-gene and linker sites.

operations.label: PCR 1
operations.description: Exponentially amplify the linker-bearing TCR template using constant-gene and linker anchors; a biotinylated constant-gene primer marks products for recapture.
operations.mechanism: First of the two exponential PCR rounds described for the constant-gene/ssLC primer system.
operations.information_effect: Increases copies of the TCR-derived insert, including CDR3.

operations.label: Magnetic capture and strand release (PCR 1 → PCR 2 interface)
operations.description: Recapture the biotinylated first-round PCR products on magnetic beads, then denature the duplexes to obtain their non-biotinylated strands for PCR 2. The poster shows a bead at PCR 1 and a bead-free PCR 2 product; these intermediate transformations are resolved by the primary method text.
operations.mechanism: Additional magnetic capture of the biotinylated product followed by NaOH denaturation to recover non-biotinylated strands.
operations.information_effect: Provides an enrichment and strand-transfer interface between rounds; the released strand preserves the TCR insert and primer-site information. The paper describes increased specificity, not perfect biological specificity.

operations.label: PCR 2 with nested primers
operations.description: Use the released first-round template for a second exponential amplification with nested constant-gene and ssLC primers, yielding bead-free TCR amplicons.
operations.mechanism: Nested primer selection within the same constant-gene/linker architecture.
operations.information_effect: Further selects and amplifies the TCR region including CDR3; this operation neither fuses α and β chains nor introduces a per-cell association.

operations.label: Add sequencing adapters

operations.information_effect: Makes TCR-derived amplicons sequenceable and supports sample assignment. Sample barcodes are distinct from receptor identity and do not establish molecule counts or α–β pairing.

method_scopes.rationale: All operations belong to the one expanded method named by the middle row. The primary paper explicitly names TCR-LA-MC PCR and describes the same constant-gene biotin priming, bead capture, ssLC ligation, two-PCR architecture and subsequent sequencing-adaptor addition. The separate Illumina adapter block and bead-bearing PCR 1 interface select the described main workflow with a MiSeq interface, rather than the paper’s comparison variants that omit the second capture or add adapters during PCR 2. α and β are biological chain targets within this one schematic; their complete implementations need not be identical, and the drawing supplies no separate branch operations to assign. Magnetic capture is a component of TCR-LA-MC PCR, not a separate target assay.
